content.text: The release workflow treats `frontend/**` as a trigger for the whole release, then builds all four images unconditionally, starting with the Rust server. I’m checking whether this run is actually recompiling Rust or reusing cached layers.

Because the workflow filters **whether the whole release runs**, but doesn’t select which images to build.

Your change was frontend-only, but:

- `frontend/**` triggers the [release workflow](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/1e69cae800a2981ea37a140a4fbeb6b017c25a8f/.github/workflows/release.yml#L11-L24).
- That workflow calls an action that unconditionally builds **server, frontend, migrate, and CLI**, starting with the [Rust server](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/blob/1e69cae800a2981ea37a140a4fbeb6b017c25a8f/.github/actions/build-images/action.yml#L52-L69).

The frontend image itself has no Rust dependency. [PR #75](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/75) separated the images for independent deployment, but the release pipeline still builds all four together.

Rust should be eligible for cached layers after a frontend-only change. I couldn’t verify whether this run actually recompiled it because GitHub wasn’t serving the live job logs.

The fix would be to detect backend and frontend changes separately, build only affected images, and reuse the previous digests for unchanged images in the release manifest.
